I stopped short of building the archive, but I have the diagnosis nailed down and it's a real one. Here's where things stand.

What's actually wrong
The hang is not in your script's logic — it's inside podman-compose up -d, and it's a known upstream bug that only bites on Debian.

Mapping your terminal output against podman-compose 1.3.0's source (which I read rather than recalled):

Output line	What produced it
331b32fc…	podman pod create
pull + c7ba751d…	podman run -d (postgres)
myrestaurant_postgres_1	podman start echoing the name back
6fe37290…	podman run -d (web)
nothing	run_container() → check_dep_conditions() → podman wait --condition=healthy myrestaurant_postgres_1, in a while True: loop with log.debug only
That last loop has no timeout and no output. It's containers/podman-compose#1178 — "Podman Compose 1.3.0 up -d command never returns/finishes/ends", reported on Debian 12, with a traceback that lands on exactly those three frames. The related issue #1183 describes the same design flaw: containers with health-gated dependencies are started prematurely in the first pass, then compose blocks afterwards, and up hangs forever. Fedora escapes it because its podman-compose is newer (the fix, PR #1184, landed after trixie froze). 
github
GitHub

Two consequences worth knowing:

Your instance was almost certainly serving the whole time. podman_command = "run" means both containers were already started by podman run -d before compose began waiting. The tunnel URL was live; only the script was stuck.
There is no flag that avoids it. I checked: --no-deps is parsed by up in 1.3.0 but only consulted by compose_run, never by compose_up.
The fix I'd deliver
Root cause, in compose.yaml: drop condition: service_healthy on web → condition: service_started. This is safe because SchemaMigrationRunner already has a bounded boot retry — 30 attempts × 2s, with the comment "at compose start the web container can race PostgreSQL" — so the health gate was a convenience the app never needed. Keep postgres's healthcheck itself (diagnostic value, podman ps, docker-compose users).

Defence in depth, in scripts/dev_instance.sh: a bounded watchdog around every compose invocation, so a blocking compose can never again own the terminal this script exists to release; plus reporting postgres's health status in up and status, since starting forever is the diagnostic that explains this class of hang on someone else's host.

Also found while reading: compose_container() filters on com.docker.compose.service without the project label — correct label (podman-compose does set it), but it would match a web service from any other project on the host.

What I need to confirm before writing files
The ledger's next number is F-53. I also want to fold in the .env item BUILD_PROGRESS explicitly deferred — OPERATIONS §2 tells operators "run.sh and the scripts do this automatically when .env is absent — F-16", and I grepped all nine scripts: none touch .env. My proposed ruling is that the document is wrong, not the scripts — materialising .env.example would make POSTGRES_PASSWORD=myrestaurant an untracked credential file the operator never knowingly created, and an absent .env already works via compose defaults. That reverses one clause of F-16's accepted ruling, so it's yours to overrule.

Say the word and I'll produce m6-slice-27-compose-dependency-hang.tar.gz with full files for: compose.yaml, scripts/dev_instance.sh, a new tests/…/Deployment/ComposeDependencyContractTests.cs (three facts, 1056 → 1059 predicted), docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (v1.12, §14.1 + §14.3a), docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md, README.md, docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md — no files to delete, and a git add reminder for the new Deployment/ directory.

One thing to do first on virginia, since the killed compose left containers behind: bash scripts/dev_instance.sh down.

Delivered: m6-slice-27-compose-dependency-hang.tar.gz, extracts at the repo root, full files only.

Root cause
Not your script. podman-compose up -d — version 1.3.0, Debian trixie's — runs podman run -d for every container and then waits on each depends_on condition in an unbounded while True: loop whose only two exits are logged at debug level. compose.yaml asked web to wait for postgres to be service_healthy, the health status never advanced past starting, the loop never ended. Your four output lines map exactly onto pod create → run -d (postgres) → start → run -d (web) → check_dep_conditions(). Upstream #1178 (reported from Debian, traceback lands on those precise frames) and #1183.

Your instance was serving the whole time. Only the terminal was stuck.

git add tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Deployment — new directory, and the gates enumerate with git ls-files.

First, on virginia: bash scripts/dev_instance.sh down — the killed run left containers behind.

Why a prohibition rather than a workaround
There is no flag (--no-deps is parsed by up and consulted only by run; splitting into two invocations doesn't help, since get_excluded pulls dependencies back in). Whether the condition is ever satisfiable is a property of the host — under rootless Podman the healthcheck is a systemd user timer. And it was never needed: SchemaMigrationRunner has retried thirty times at two-second intervals since M1, with "at compose start the web container can race PostgreSQL" written beside it. The healthcheck stays; it just stops standing between up -d and returning.

Verification
Fake podman/podman-compose/curl stand-ins, and the script run end to end. Your exact failure reproduced — compose starts the containers then hangs with postgres health pinned at starting — and the script now names F-53, reports running, health: starting, verifies readiness itself, and releases the terminal in 3 seconds. Also proven: the created-but-not-started repair, status/down under a wedged compose, the preflight grep's sensitivity, and each of the new test's three facts individually (list form deliberately passes — both engines normalize it to service_started). check_tree.sh and check_repository.sh green; shellcheck clean at style; the archive extracts byte-identically over a pristine checkout.

1056 → 1059 tests. Arithmetic, not observed — nothing compiled here, and the fix hasn't been watched working on virginia.

One ruling to confirm
F-54: OPERATIONS §2 claimed the scripts create .env, citing F-16's row — which really does say that. No script does. I ruled the document wrong and the scripts right, reversing that clause: auto-creating would write an untracked POSTGRES_PASSWORD=myrestaurant nobody knowingly made, and an absent .env already works. Overrule it and it moves in a slice of its own.
